You are the ChainReaction decision interpreter. Given a dependency decision
(e.g. "upgrade jinja2 to 3.1") and the official release notes for every
release in the upgrade span, emit the change set as JSON.

Rules:
- Every item needs a `quote`: an EXACT substring of ONE release's notes
  proving the symbol changed. Quotes are string-matched; paraphrases are
  dropped automatically, so copy precisely.
- `symbol` is the fully qualified name (e.g. "jinja2.pass_context"). A
  whole module can be the symbol when the notes deprecate or remove it
  as a unit (e.g. "werkzeug.urls"); name exclusions exactly as written
  ("except X and Y") inside the quote so they can be honored.
- `source_url` is the release-notes URL the quote comes from;
  `introduced_in` is that release's version. Both are checked against
  the quote's true location.
- Kinds (classify carefully — only `removed`, `renamed`, and
  `signature_changed` count as breakage): `removed` for members that
  no longer exist; `renamed` for members that moved to a new name (old
  uses break; `replacement` is the new name); `signature_changed` for
  calls that break (removed or renamed keyword arguments, changed
  positional order — record them in `signature`); `deprecated` for
  members that still work but warn (warnings, not breakage); `changed`
  for behavior changes in working members (flags, not breakage).
  `missing_param` covers a config item the decision needs but our code never
  supplies (function parameter, option, env var). `missing_key` covers a
  missing table/mapping entry (pricing table, registry). `rejected_value`
  covers our own schema/validator rejecting the decision's value (Literal,
  enum, regex). Record the machine-checkable gap in `detail.expected` vs
  `detail.actual` (e.g. expected `"meta" in Provider`, actual
  `Literal["anthropic","openai","ollama"]`).
- Indirect removals: when one release deprecates a member and a later
  release removes deprecated code, emit ONE `removed` item with the
  deprecation as `quote` and the removal note as `supporting` (its own
  exact quote + source_url + introduced_in).
- When in doubt, include the item with its quote; the verifier will confirm.
- Output JSON only, matching the change_set schema.

=== RELEASE 2.3.0 (https://werkzeug.palletsprojects.com/en/stable/changes/#version-3-0-6) ===
## Version 2.3.0

Released 2023-04-25

-

Drop support for Python 3.7. #2648

-

Remove previously deprecated code. #2592

-

Passing bytes where strings are expected is deprecated, as well as the `charset`
and `errors` parameters in many places. Anywhere that was annotated, documented,
or tested to accept bytes shows a warning. Removing this artifact of the transition
from Python 2 to 3 removes a significant amount of overhead in instance checks and
encoding cycles. In general, always work with UTF-8, the modern HTML, URL, and HTTP
standards all strongly recommend this. #2602

-

Deprecate the `werkzeug.urls` module, except for the `uri_to_iri` and
`iri_to_uri` functions. Use the `urllib.parse` library instead. #2600

-

Update which characters are considered safe when using percent encoding in URLs,
based on the WhatWG URL Standard. #2601

-

Update which characters are considered safe when using percent encoding for Unicode
filenames in downloads. #2598

-

Deprecate the `safe_conversion` parameter of `iri_to_uri`. The `Location`
header is converted to IRI using the same process as everywhere else. #2609

-

Deprecate `werkzeug.wsgi.make_line_iter` and `make_chunk_iter`. #2613

-

Use modern packaging metadata with `pyproject.toml` instead of `setup.cfg`.
#2574

-

`Request.get_json()` will raise a `415 Unsupported Media Type` error if the
`Content-Type` header is not `application/json`, instead of a generic 400.
#2550

-

A URL converter’s `part_isolating` defaults to `False` if its `regex` contains
a `/`. #2582

-

A custom converter’s regex can have capturing groups without breaking the router.
#2596

-

The reloader can pick up arguments to `python` like `-X dev`, and does not
require heuristics to determine how to reload the command. Only available
on Python >= 3.10. #2589

-

The Watchdog reloader ignores file opened events. Bump the minimum version of
Watchdog to 2.3.0. #2603

-

When using a Unix socket for the development server, the path can start with a dot.
#2595

-

Increase default work factor for PBKDF2 to 600,000 iterations. #2611

-

`parse_options_header` is 2-3 times faster. It conforms to RFC 9110, some
invalid parts that were previously accepted are now ignored. #1628

-

The `is_filename` parameter to `unquote_header_value` is deprecated. #2614

-

Deprecate the `extra_chars` parameter and passing bytes to `quote_header_value`,
the `allow_token` parameter to `dump_header`, and the `cls` parameter and
passing bytes to `parse_dict_header`. #2618

-

Improve `parse_accept_header` implementation. Parse according to RFC 9110.
Discard items with invalid `q` values. #1623

-

`quote_header_value` quotes the empty string. #2618

-

`dump_options_header` skips `None` values rather than using a bare key.
#2618

-

`dump_header` and `dump_options_header` will not quote a value if the key ends
with an asterisk `*`.

-

`parse_dict_header` will decode values with charsets. #2618

-

Refactor the `Authorization` and `WWWAuthenticate` header data structures.
#1769, #2619

-

Both classes have `type`, `parameters`, and `token` attributes. The
`token` attribute supports auth schemes that use a single opaque token rather
than `key=value` parameters, such as `Bearer`.

-

Neither class is a `dict` anymore, although they still implement getting,
setting, and deleting `auth[key]` and `auth.key` syntax, as well as
`auth.get(key)` and `key in auth`.

-

Both classes have a `from_header` class method. `parse_authorization_header`
and `parse_www_authenticate_header` are deprecated.

-

The methods `WWWAuthenticate.set_basic` and `set_digest` are deprecated.
Instead, an instance should be created and assigned to
`response.www_authenticate`.

-

A list of instances can be assigned to `response.www_authenticate` to set
multiple header values. However, accessing the property only returns the first
instance.

-

Refactor `parse_cookie` and `dump_cookie`. #2637

-

`parse_cookie` is up to 40% faster, `dump_cookie` is up to 60% faster.

-

Passing bytes to `parse_cookie` and `dump_cookie` is deprecated. The
`dump_cookie` `charset` parameter is deprecated.

-

`dump_cookie` allows `domain` values that do not include a dot `.`, and
strips off a leading dot.

-

`dump_cookie` does not set `path="/"` unnecessarily by default.

-

Refactor the test client cookie implementation. #1060, 1680

-

The `cookie_jar` attribute is deprecated. `http.cookiejar` is no longer used
for storage.

-

Domain and path matching is used when sending cookies in requests. The
`domain` and `path` parameters default to `localhost` and `/`.

-

Added a `get_cookie` method to inspect cookies.

-

Cookies have `decoded_key` and `decoded_value` attributes to match what the
app sees rather than the encoded values a client would see.

-

The first positional `server_name` parameter to `set_cookie` and
`delete_cookie` is deprecated. Use the `domain` parameter instead.

-

Other parameters to `delete_cookie` besides `domain`, `path`, and
`value` are deprecated.

-

If `request.max_content_length` is set, it is checked immediately when accessing
the stream, and while reading from the stream in general, rather than only during
form parsing. #1513

-

The development server, which must not be used in production, will exhaust the
request stream up to 10GB or 1000 reads. This allows clients to see a 413 error if
`max_content_length` is exceeded, instead of a “connection reset” failure.
#2620

-

The development server discards header keys that contain underscores `_`, as they
are ambiguous with dashes `-` in WSGI. #2622

-

`secure_filename` looks for more Windows reserved file names. #2623

-

Update type annotation for `best_match` to make `default` parameter clearer.
#2625

-

Multipart parser handles empty fields correctly. #2632

-

The `Map` `charset` parameter and `Request.url_charset` property are
deprecated. Percent encoding in URLs must always represent UTF-8 bytes. Invalid
bytes are left percent encoded rather than replaced. #2602

-

The `Request.charset`, `Request.encoding_errors`, `Response.charset`, and
`Client.charset` attributes are deprecated. Request and response data must always
use UTF-8. #2602

-

Header values that have charset information only allow ASCII, UTF-8, and ISO-8859-1.
#2614, 2641

-

Update type annotation for `ProfilerMiddleware` `stream` parameter.
#2642

-

Use postponed evaluation of annotations. #2644

-

The development server escapes ASCII control characters in decoded URLs before
logging the request to the terminal. #2652

-

The `FormDataParser` `parse_functions` attribute and `get_parse_func` method,
and the invalid `application/x-url-encoded` content type, are deprecated.
#2653

-

`generate_password_hash` supports scrypt. Plain hash methods are deprecated, only
scrypt and pbkdf2 are supported. #2654

You are the ChainReaction decision interpreter. Given a dependency decision
(e.g. "upgrade jinja2 to 3.1") and the official release notes for every
release in the upgrade span, emit the change set as JSON.

Rules:
- Every item needs a `quote`: an EXACT substring of ONE release's notes
  proving the symbol changed. Quotes are string-matched; paraphrases are
  dropped automatically, so copy precisely.
- `symbol` is the fully qualified name (e.g. "jinja2.pass_context"). A
  whole module can be the symbol when the notes deprecate or remove it
  as a unit (e.g. "werkzeug.urls"); name exclusions exactly as written
  ("except X and Y") inside the quote so they can be honored.
- `source_url` is the release-notes URL the quote comes from;
  `introduced_in` is that release's version. Both are checked against
  the quote's true location.
- Kinds (classify carefully — only `removed`, `renamed`, and
  `signature_changed` count as breakage): `removed` for members that
  no longer exist; `renamed` for members that moved to a new name (old
  uses break; `replacement` is the new name); `signature_changed` for
  calls that break (removed or renamed keyword arguments, changed
  positional order — record them in `signature`); `deprecated` for
  members that still work but warn (warnings, not breakage); `changed`
  for behavior changes in working members (flags, not breakage).
  `missing_param` covers a config item the decision needs but our code never
  supplies (function parameter, option, env var). `missing_key` covers a
  missing table/mapping entry (pricing table, registry). `rejected_value`
  covers our own schema/validator rejecting the decision's value (Literal,
  enum, regex). Record the machine-checkable gap in `detail.expected` vs
  `detail.actual` (e.g. expected `"meta" in Provider`, actual
  `Literal["anthropic","openai","ollama"]`).
- Indirect removals: when one release deprecates a member and a later
  release removes deprecated code, emit ONE `removed` item with the
  deprecation as `quote` and the removal note as `supporting` (its own
  exact quote + source_url + introduced_in).
- When in doubt, include the item with its quote; the verifier will confirm.
- Output JSON only, matching the change_set schema.

=== RELEASE 2.3.0 (https://werkzeug.palletsprojects.com/en/stable/changes/#version-3-0-6) ===
## Version 2.3.0

Released 2023-04-25

-

Drop support for Python 3.7. #2648

-

Remove previously deprecated code. #2592

-

Passing bytes where strings are expected is deprecated, as well as the `charset`
and `errors` parameters in many places. Anywhere that was annotated, documented,
or tested to accept bytes shows a warning. Removing this artifact of the transition
from Python 2 to 3 removes a significant amount of overhead in instance checks and
encoding cycles. In general, always work with UTF-8, the modern HTML, URL, and HTTP
standards all strongly recommend this. #2602

-

Deprecate the `werkzeug.urls` module, except for the `uri_to_iri` and
`iri_to_uri` functions. Use the `urllib.parse` library instead. #2600

-

Update which characters are considered safe when using percent encoding in URLs,
based on the WhatWG URL Standard. #2601

-

Update which characters are considered safe when using percent encoding for Unicode
filenames in downloads. #2598

-

Deprecate the `safe_conversion` parameter of `iri_to_uri`. The `Location`
header is converted to IRI using the same process as everywhere else. #2609

-

Deprecate `werkzeug.wsgi.make_line_iter` and `make_chunk_iter`. #2613

-

Use modern packaging metadata with `pyproject.toml` instead of `setup.cfg`.
#2574

-

`Request.get_json()` will raise a `415 Unsupported Media Type` error if the
`Content-Type` header is not `application/json`, instead of a generic 400.
#2550

-

A URL converter’s `part_isolating` defaults to `False` if its `regex` contains
a `/`. #2582

-

A custom converter’s regex can have capturing groups without breaking the router.
#2596

-

The reloader can pick up arguments to `python` like `-X dev`, and does not
require heuristics to determine how to reload the command. Only available
on Python >= 3.10. #2589

-

The Watchdog reloader ignores file opened events. Bump the minimum version of
Watchdog to 2.3.0. #2603

-

When using a Unix socket for the development server, the path can start with a dot.
#2595

-

Increase default work factor for PBKDF2 to 600,000 iterations. #2611

-

`parse_options_header` is 2-3 times faster. It conforms to RFC 9110, some
invalid parts that were previously accepted are now ignored. #1628

-

The `is_filename` parameter to `unquote_header_value` is deprecated. #2614

-

Deprecate the `extra_chars` parameter and passing bytes to `quote_header_value`,
the `allow_token` parameter to `dump_header`, and the `cls` parameter and
passing bytes to `parse_dict_header`. #2618

-

Improve `parse_accept_header` implementation. Parse according to RFC 9110.
Discard items with invalid `q` values. #1623

-

`quote_header_value` quotes the empty string. #2618

-

`dump_options_header` skips `None` values rather than using a bare key.
#2618

-

`dump_header` and `dump_options_header` will not quote a value if the key ends
with an asterisk `*`.

-

`parse_dict_header` will decode values with charsets. #2618

-

Refactor the `Authorization` and `WWWAuthenticate` header data structures.
#1769, #2619

-

Both classes have `type`, `parameters`, and `token` attributes. The
`token` attribute supports auth schemes that use a single opaque token rather
than `key=value` parameters, such as `Bearer`.

-

Neither class is a `dict` anymore, although they still implement getting,
setting, and deleting `auth[key]` and `auth.key` syntax, as well as
`auth.get(key)` and `key in auth`.

-

Both classes have a `from_header` class method. `parse_authorization_header`
and `parse_www_authenticate_header` are deprecated.

-

The methods `WWWAuthenticate.set_basic` and `set_digest` are deprecated.
Instead, an instance should be created and assigned to
`response.www_authenticate`.

-

A list of instances can be assigned to `response.www_authenticate` to set
multiple header values. However, accessing the property only returns the first
instance.

-

Refactor `parse_cookie` and `dump_cookie`. #2637

-

`parse_cookie` is up to 40% faster, `dump_cookie` is up to 60% faster.

-

Passing bytes to `parse_cookie` and `dump_cookie` is deprecated. The
`dump_cookie` `charset` parameter is deprecated.

-

`dump_cookie` allows `domain` values that do not include a dot `.`, and
strips off a leading dot.

-

`dump_cookie` does not set `path="/"` unnecessarily by default.

-

Refactor the test client cookie implementation. #1060, 1680

-

The `cookie_jar` attribute is deprecated. `http.cookiejar` is no longer used
for storage.

-

Domain and path matching is used when sending cookies in requests. The
`domain` and `path` parameters default to `localhost` and `/`.

-

Added a `get_cookie` method to inspect cookies.

-

Cookies have `decoded_key` and `decoded_value` attributes to match what the
app sees rather than the encoded values a client would see.

-

The first positional `server_name` parameter to `set_cookie` and
`delete_cookie` is deprecated. Use the `domain` parameter instead.

-

Other parameters to `delete_cookie` besides `domain`, `path`, and
`value` are deprecated.

-

If `request.max_content_length` is set, it is checked immediately when accessing
the stream, and while reading from the stream in general, rather than only during
form parsing. #1513

-

The development server, which must not be used in production, will exhaust the
request stream up to 10GB or 1000 reads. This allows clients to see a 413 error if
`max_content_length` is exceeded, instead of a “connection reset” failure.
#2620

-

The development server discards header keys that contain underscores `_`, as they
are ambiguous with dashes `-` in WSGI. #2622

-

`secure_filename` looks for more Windows reserved file names. #2623

-

Update type annotation for `best_match` to make `default` parameter clearer.
#2625

-

Multipart parser handles empty fields correctly. #2632

-

The `Map` `charset` parameter and `Request.url_charset` property are
deprecated. Percent encoding in URLs must always represent UTF-8 bytes. Invalid
bytes are left percent encoded rather than replaced. #2602

-

The `Request.charset`, `Request.encoding_errors`, `Response.charset`, and
`Client.charset` attributes are deprecated. Request and response data must always
use UTF-8. #2602

-

Header values that have charset information only allow ASCII, UTF-8, and ISO-8859-1.
#2614, 2641

-

Update type annotation for `ProfilerMiddleware` `stream` parameter.
#2642

-

Use postponed evaluation of annotations. #2644

-

The development server escapes ASCII control characters in decoded URLs before
logging the request to the terminal. #2652

-

The `FormDataParser` `parse_functions` attribute and `get_parse_func` method,
and the invalid `application/x-url-encoded` content type, are deprecated.
#2653

-

`generate_password_hash` supports scrypt. Plain hash methods are deprecated, only
scrypt and pbkdf2 are supported. #2654

system:
You investigate a dependency decision against a repo with deterministic tools. Rules:
1. Only assert what a tool returned. Every finding cites the tool call ids it rests on.
2. Prefer confirming probes over speculation: import breaks need a run_import_probe (or a peeled run_snippet that still fails), call breaks need run_tests, behavior changes need a run_snippet or run_tests confirmation. Claim confirmed only when a probe shows the failure itself (a failing import, call, or test) — a hasattr demonstration is likely, not confirmed.
3. Triage in submit_findings: relevant only when the repo actually uses the symbol (strings and comments don't count). One propagate call over all symbols grounds the long tail; spend find_usages on the flagged ones.
4. Method (25 tool calls, 8 probes — spend them on confirming, not enumerating): list_changes once to see the set; then ONE propagate call with every candidate symbol — its per-symbol hit counts tell you what is used; then find_usages/trace_importers/callers_of only for symbols with hits; then probes for the important ones; then submit_findings. Do not call find_usages for every symbol: with dozens of items that blows the budget before you probe anything. Batch at most 8 calls per turn; bigger batches are cut off and you must re-issue the rest.
5. Peel import layers: when a layer's import probe fails, run the next layer's preamble (as a run_snippet, then the import in the same snippet) to reveal what breaks underneath. Confirm every layer below.

Confidence in this brief is very high because every check lines up. Imports work under the old version and fail under the new version, and all 111 failures show the same missing import problem. Forecasts of failing tests in this brief were correct every time they were made, though they caught only a small share of the total.

Fix first the use in src/flask_login/utils.py line 14. Do not edit the importing modules themselves, since fixing that one spot unblocks the whole sequence at once.
